summary: Adds a `--retries` option to the command line and a greeting step to CI. The option works for the usual case, but both new shell commands run text that an outside contributor controls, so this cannot merge as is.

findings.title: The pull request title is run as shell code in CI
findings.body: `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` is expanded into the script before the shell parses it, so a title such as `"; curl …| sh; echo "` runs arbitrary commands on the runner with this job's token. Pass it through an environment variable instead; the shell then treats it as data.
findings.suggestion:
- name: Greet
        env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          echo "Testing $TITLE"

findings.title: `shell=True` runs the name argument as a command
findings.body: `widgets 'x; rm -rf ~'` runs `rm -rf ~`: the f-string puts the argument into a shell command line. Pass a list and let `subprocess` quote nothing. `check=True` also makes a failed fetch visible instead of printing the greeting anyway.

findings.title: Every retry runs even after a fetch succeeds
findings.body: The loop has no exit, so the default `--retries 3` fetches three times on every call. Stop after the first success, and re-raise the last error once the attempts are used up.

findings.title: The README still shows the old usage
findings.body: `README.md:12` documents `widgets NAME` only. The project's CONTRIBUTING asks for user-facing options to be documented in the same pull request.

findings.title: Note the removal of `db/legacy.sql` in the changelog
findings.body: The file was the only record of how the old table was dropped. One line in `CHANGELOG.md` keeps that history findable.

findings.title: No test covers `--retries`
findings.body: `tests/test_cli.py` exercises only the name argument. A test with a fake `widget-fetch` that fails once would pin down the retry behaviour fixed above.

findings.title: `attempt` is never used
findings.body: Name the loop variable `_`, as the rest of the package does.

checked: `parse_args(argv)` keeps `main()` callable from tests, as the package's other entry points are
The new step runs on the same runner image and Python version as the existing ones
